login.subtitle: MCP Platform
login.title: Sign in to <brand>xtweetly</brand>
login.sentDesc: Login link sent to {email}. Valid for 15 minutes.

connectDialog.emailPlaceholder: Sometimes required if X asks for extra verification
connectDialog.passwordHint: Encrypted with AES-256-GCM; cleared as soon as login completes.
connectDialog.passwordLoginBody: Your X account is connected through our secure browser session. You do not need to paste tokens or cookies manually.
connectDialog.totpHint: X → Settings → Security → 2FA → Authenticator app → the base32 string under "Can't scan the QR". Not the 6-digit code.
connectDialog.saveTotpHint: When on, we can auto-reauth if the session drops.
connectDialog.durationHint: This usually takes 30–90 seconds. X sometimes asks for extra verification — that adds time.
connectDialog.alreadyConnectedBody: <handle>@{accountId}</handle> is already connected. Open the Accounts page and use this account's "Re-authenticate" button to refresh its session.
connectDialog.cooldownManualTitle: Too many recent failures — manual review needed
connectDialog.cooldownManualBody: {count} failed attempts in a row. Wait at least {countdown}; if it keeps failing, ask support for manual review.
connectDialog.cancellingHint: Asking the worker to stop. This usually completes within a few seconds.
connectDialog.cancelledBody: The login attempt was stopped. No account changes were made.

failureReasons.invalid_credentials: Wrong username or password. Confirm you can sign in to x.com manually, then try again.
failureReasons.captcha_required: X showed a captcha challenge. Verify the account on x.com or wait a bit, then try again.
failureReasons.email_challenge: X asked for an "unusual login" verification step. Add the account email and try again; if 2FA is enabled, provide the base32 secret too.
failureReasons.email_verification_required: X asked for an email or verification code. Complete that verification on x.com, then try again.
failureReasons.suspicious_login_blocked: X flagged this login as suspicious. Sign in manually from the same IP/region, confirm the account, then try again.
failureReasons.login_cooldown: X detected too many login attempts. Wait 30–60 minutes and try again.
failureReasons.cookies_missing: Login completed but the X session cookies couldn't be captured. Wait a moment and retry; if it keeps happening, ask support for manual review.
failureReasons.home_not_reached: We submitted the password but X didn't take us to the home page. It likely asked for extra verification or applied a soft block.
failureReasons.account_locked: X has locked this account. Sign in to x.com directly, complete the on-screen steps (phone verify, email confirm, etc.), then try again.
failureReasons.phone_verification_required: X requires phone verification. Complete it on x.com, then try connecting again.
failureReasons.unknown: Unexpected error. Wait a moment and retry; if it persists, ask support for manual review.

guide.title: Quick Start
guide.subtitle: Connect xtweetly to Claude Code in 5 minutes.
guide.step1Desc: Start the secure connection flow from the Accounts page with your X username and password. No manual token or cookie entry is needed.
guide.step2Desc: Create a new key from the API Keys page. Select "Full Access". You'll see the key only once — copy it immediately.
guide.step3Desc: Go to your Dashboard — it shows the ready-to-paste command with your actual server URL and API key prefix pre-filled.
guide.step4Desc: Just ask Claude naturally — it will pick the right tool:
guide.trouble1: Invalid API key: make sure it starts with tk_.
guide.trouble2: MCP not connecting: verify the URL — copy it fresh from the Dashboard.
guide.trouble3: Action failed: check error details on the /actions page.
guide.allClientsSetup: Setup for all clients (Claude Desktop, ChatGPT, Cursor, …)

docs.title: xtweetly <accent>API</accent>
docs.subtitle: Interactive API reference powered by Scalar, served live from the backend. Every route documented, every error envelope spelled out — the same OpenAPI 3.1 spec our MCP tools are generated from.

envWarning.title: Backend URL not configured
envWarning.body: Set NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL in your environment to point this page (and every Docs link) at your live backend. In production it's usually something like https://api.your-domain.com.

surface.title: What you can do over HTTP.
surface.body: Bearer-token auth, JSON in/out, deterministic error envelopes, and an idempotency contract on every write endpoint. Pick your client — REST, MCP, or the generated SDK.
surface.moreLink: + 23 more · open API Reference for the full list

clients.title: Pick your client
clients.helper: OAuth clients authenticate in the browser — no API key needed. For CLI / legacy clients, use a tk_ key.

noAccount.title: Don't have an account?
noAccount.body: Sign in with a magic link in 30 seconds — connect your X account, then come back here for API key or OAuth flow.

developer.title: Building your own MCP client?
developer.body: Standard MCP 2025-06-18 + RFC 9728 + RFC 8414. Discovery starts at /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource. PKCE S256 required; refresh tokens not yet issued (tk_* are long-lived).
